articles.title: Housing crisis leads to snap election in Spain
articles.author: Ana Vračar
articles.content_excerpt: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez announced a snap election for late November after two housing bills were defeated in a parliamentary vote on Friday, October 2. The bills came amid widespread mass mobilizations demanding urgent action on the country’s housing crisis, following the eviction of an 87-year-old woman in Madrid. articles.title: Iran welcomes the withdrawal of US forces from Iraq, calling it a victory for the resistance
articles.author: Abdul Rahman
articles.content_excerpt: The withdrawal of the remaining US troops from Iraq is a victory for the Iraqi nation and the resistance force in the region, Iran claimed on Thursday, October 1, also calling for greater cooperation between both the countries to achieve complete sovereignty for Iraq. “The US, despite possessing vast resources and equipment, has been expelled from Iraq, and the Iraqi people are celebrating this victory,” head of Iran’s Quds’ forces Esmail Qaani said during a program held in Tehran to mark the second anniversary of the Israeli assassination of Hezbollah leader Hasan Nasrallah. He thanked the “resistance of the Iraqi nation and the heroes of the Resistance Front” for making the end of the US occupation a reality. articles.title: The first national gold refinery: How Burkina Faso’s mining revolution advances its struggle for sovereignty
articles.author: Pavan Kulkarni
articles.content_excerpt: After expanding domestic control over mining to pursue economic sovereignty, Burkina Faso has moved up the value chain with its first gold refinery, inaugurated by its president, Capt. Ibrahim Traoré, on September 28. Most of the gold mined in the country was previously exported as unrefined dore to be processed abroad. articles.title: Far Right Makes Gains in Brazil as Flávio Bolsonaro Tops Lula in First Round of Presidential Race
articles.content_excerpt: This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form. AMY GOODMAN : We begin today’s show in Brazil, where the presidential race between President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and far-right Senator Flávio Bolsonaro is headed to a runoff. During the first round of voting Sunday, Bolsonaro received 47% of the vote; Lula got 45%. Bolsonaro is the son of Brazil’s former far-right President Jair Bolsonaro, currently under house arrest serving a 27-year sentence after he was convicted of plotting a military coup in 2022 to overturn Lula’s win in that year’s election. articles.title: “I Am Jane Doe”: Cornell Case Reignites Debate over Rape Culture, Frats & Prosecuting Sex Crimes
articles.content_excerpt: Revelations of sexual assault at a Cornell University fraternity in 2024 and how the university responded have sparked national outrage, reigniting a public debate about “the extent to which fraternities, the extent to which athletics really support this kind of culture that allows perpetrators to escape with little or no accountability,” says law professor Deborah Tuerkheimer. In 2024, seven male students avoided criminal prosecution after allegedly drugging and gang-raping a female student at the Chi Phi fraternity house. Cornell is now under intense scrutiny for its handling of the original investigation, which found that the student identified as Jane Doe was sexually assaulted by two of seven men, resulting in expulsions for two and lesser consequences for the other five. articles.title: Meet Issa Amro: Palestinian Human Rights Advocate Attacked by Settlers, Detained by Israeli Army
articles.content_excerpt: We speak with Palestinian human rights defender Issa Amro after he was detained at an Israeli military base for seven hours on Friday. Amro, the founder of the Hebron-based group Youth Against Settlements, was helping a Palestinian family that he says had been attacked by armed Israeli settlers at their farmhouse outside Hebron in the occupied West Bank. Amro says when Israeli soldiers arrived, they ignored the settlers and instead targeted the Palestinians, including him. Amro tells Democracy Now! that soldiers handcuffed and blindfolded him before transporting him to the base in the back of a military vehicle. articles.author: Michael Roberts
articles.content_excerpt: As the Tax Foundation correctly points out, total national income is not made up just of profits and wages received but also from depreciation. articles.title: How United Airlines became a link in Israel’s weapons supply chain
articles.author: Zoe Alexandra
articles.content_excerpt: United Airlines has been sending military hardware to Israel on passenger flights, right under your feet. A new report from the People’s Embargo for Palestine, the Palestinian Youth Movement, and others documents 2,761 shipments of military cargo to Israeli weapons manufacturers and military institutions, including Elbit Systems, Lockheed Martin Israel, Nevatim Airbase, and the Israeli Ministry of Defense.
